cards.title: Designing Preclinical Regimens to Match a Qualified Reference Exposure Profile
cards.claim: When an appropriate reference concentration-time profile is available, simulate candidate animal regimens to compare profile shape and exposure with the reference, including the consequences of different terminal half-lives. Evaluate experimental feasibility alongside matching quality; the selected animal regimen remains study-specific.
conditions: A qualified reference profile for the intended analyte, matrix, total/free basis and regimen is explicitly supplied.
The animal PK model is qualified within the route, dose and study-state range used in the design.
This method does not create human reference data for a target lacking human PK.
required_inputs: Reference profile or distribution with provenance, regimen, units, matrix and exposure window.
Animal PK model, parameter uncertainty, actual dosing constraints and candidate administration schedules.
Matched comparison criteria for time course, exposure and feasible sampling confirmation.
limitations: Matching plasma exposure does not guarantee matched tissue exposure or PD response.
Different disease states or nonlinear PK can invalidate simple schedule translation.
No source dose, dosing interval or percentile range is a universal requirement.
cards.downstream_use: Design an explicitly bounded animal exposure-matching experiment; do not infer a human recommended dose from the matching exercise.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
